voyage.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Lanka
voyage.address: Lankamatha Road, Ragama suburb of Colombo
voyage.content: A Roman Catholic church with basilica status. The church is home to the venerated statue of Our Lady of Lanka.

voyage.name: St Luke's Anglican Church
voyage.content: The church plays an important role within the history of the Church Missionary Society on the island.

voyage.name: St Michael and All Angels Anglican Church
voyage.content: It was dedicated on 29 September 1887 and is a landmark in Kollupitiya, a suburb of Colombo, the commercial capital of Sri Lanka. A magnificent building of stone, mortar and wood.

voyage.name: St Andrew's Scots Kirk church
voyage.content: It was founded in the late 19th century, and prospered during the colonial and post-colonial periods, it was a centre for the Scots element in Colombo, the capital city of what was then Ceylon.

voyage.name: St Lucia's Cathedral
voyage.address: St Benedict's Street and St Lucia Street, Kotahena
voyage.content: The seat of the archbishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Colombo in Sri Lanka.

voyage.name: St Paul's Church (1853)
voyage.content: It is one of the oldest churches in Sri Lanka. Built by the Portuguese as a Roman Catholic church, and was known as Nossa Senhora dos Milagres

voyage.name: Buddha Jayanthi Chaithya stupa
voyage.content: A Buddhist shrine, built with reinforced concrete.

voyage.name: Gangaramaya Temple
voyage.content: One of the most important temples in Colombo. The temple's architecture is an eclectic mix of Sri Lankan, Thai, Indian and Chinese styles. And adjoining it just to the west is the Seema Malaka, another Buddhist temple complex that sits upon Beira Lake, along with Gangamaraya Park. Some urban and eccentric views of the surrounding skyline can be had from here, including looking back on the Altair Sri Lanka apartment t

voyage.name: Sri Bala Selva Vinayagar
voyage.content: Hindu temple in Colombo 10. Devoted to Shiva and Ganesh.

voyage.name: Sri Muthumariamman
voyage.content: Hindu temple in Colombo 13

voyage.name: Shiva Subramania Swami
voyage.content: Temple on Slave Island

voyage.name: Sri Ponnambalam-Vaneswaram temple
voyage.content: In Koch-chikade, 3 km north of Fort.

voyage.name: Kalani Raja Maha Viharaya.
voyage.content: Located about 9 km away from Colombo, the Kelaniya Raja Maha Viharaya is one of the most significant Buddhist temples in Sri Lanka. The temple had been built more than 2,000 years ago and contains images of reclining and preaching Buddha along with frescoes depicting incidents from his life.

voyage.name: Memm Harnafi
voyage.content: Mosque founded by C.W.W. Kannangara Mawatha.

voyage.name: Church of St Anthony
voyage.content: It is beside the sea where Sea Street and St Anthony’s Mawatha meet.

voyage.name: Jami-Ul-Alfar Mosque
voyage.content: This historic mosque is a popular tourist site. Jami-Ul-Alfar Mosque was built in 1909 by the Pettah Muslim community to fulfill their required five-times-daily prayer and Jummah on Fridays. It is one of the oldest mosques in Colombo.

voyage.name: Victoria Masonic Temple
voyage.content: It is the meeting place for the Masonic Lodges. It was built in 1901 during British rule and designed by E. Skinner, an associate of the Royal Institute of British Architects, and built by the Colombo Commercial Company. The building was built in neo-Georgian style mixed with elements of Eastern architecture.

voyage.name: Wolvendaal church
voyage.content: One of the oldest churches built during the Dutch era in 1749. The interior is decorated with Dutch furniture with the wooden carved pews, chairs, pulpit and lecterns.

voyage.name: The National Museum of Colombo
voyage.content: Department of National Museums. Also known as the Sri Lanka National Museum, it is the largest museum in Colombo. Among its exhibits, it contains regalia of the 17th-century Kandyan kings.

voyage.name: The Natural History Museum
voyage.address: Sir Marcus Fernando Mawatha, Cinnamon Gardens, Colombo 7
voyage.content: This museum features Sri Lanka's floral and fauna in dioramas.

voyage.name: The Dutch Period Museum
voyage.content: Nice but very small museum documenting Dutch colonial rule in Sri Lanka. Houses Dutch-inspired artifacts.

voyage.name: Independence Memorial Hall
voyage.content: is a national monument in Sri Lanka built for commemoration of the independence of Sri Lanka from the British rule with the establishment of Dominion of Ceylon on 4 February 1948. It also houses the Independence Memorial Museum.

voyage.name: Central Bank Currency Museum
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 8:30AM-4PM except public and bank holidays
voyage.content: Established on 20 April 1982 at the Central Bank Head Office in Colombo Fort. The Central Bank Currency Museum traces the history of the usage of coins and notes in Sri Lanka since 3 BCE and has on display a large number of old coins and notes.

voyage.name: The Sapumal Foundation
voyage.content: Colombo 7. The Sapumal Foundation was once home to the late Harry Pieris. Visitors are able to see his studio and art materials that have been left undisturbed over the years. This gallery also contains 200 paintings that follow the development of Sri Lankan art. Special art classes are also available at the gallery.

voyage.name: The Lionel Wendt Memorial Art Centre
voyage.content: The Art Centre has exhibitions, art shows and stage events. Visitors also able to purchase various antiques as well as paintings and crafts by contemporary Sri Lankan artists.

voyage.name: India House
voyage.content: The official residence in Colombo for the Indian High Commissioner in Sri Lanka. Built in 1926-27 for the Imperial Bank of India and taken over by the Government of India in 1956. It is a colonial style villa/bungalow, with large gardens along Thurstan Road. It is guarded by personnel from the Border Security Force.

voyage.name: Jefferson House
voyage.content: The ambassadorial residence in Colombo for the Ambassador of the United States in Sri Lanka. It was built in 1914 in the Cinnamon Gardens a suburb of Colombo.

voyage.name: Lakshmigiri Mansion
voyage.content: A bungalow at 102, Thurstan Road in Colombo.

voyage.name: Modera House
voyage.content: A large bungalow. A 19th-century stately home in Mutwal, north of Colombo. Now it is part of the De La Salle College.

voyage.name: Storm Lodge.
voyage.content: A mansion, owned by the Colombo Swimming Club.

voyage.name: The Lighthouse.
voyage.content: A large bungalow. Owned by the Sri Lankan Government and houses the Lakshman Kadirgamar Institute of International Relations and Strategic Studies. It is in the Cinnamon Gardens a suburb of Colombo, it was built by D. Peiris.

voyage.name: Whist Bungalow
voyage.content: A 19th-century large stately bungalow in Neoclassical style. It is in Mutwal north of Colombo on the coast where the mouth of the Kelani River used to be. It is now used as a reception hall for weddings.

voyage.name: Lotus Tower
voyage.price: $20 USD for foreigners, Rs 500 for Sri Lankans
voyage.content: Distinctive Colombo telecommunications tower that offers great views. At night, it is shining with the colours on the flower changing every few seconds.

voyage.name: Colombo Lighthouse
voyage.content: Used to look out over the pretty coastline, but now it's hemmed in by the urban centre of Colombo to the east and the new Colombo International Financial City built from reclaimed land to the west, such that it looks like an anachronism if there ever was one.

voyage.name: Galle Face Green Promenade
voyage.content: Visit at sundown for a spectacular view. The ½-km-long promenade stretches between Galle Road and the Indian Ocean; it tends to attract children, teenagers, vendors, lovers, kite flyers, merrymakers, and families. Usually on Saturday and Sunday evenings, the land is filled with day-trippers, food vendors, and people picnicking which make it very crowded. It is also the largest open space in the city.

voyage.name: Colombo Zoological Gardens
voyage.price: For overseas visitors: adult Rs 2000, child Rs 1000, video cameras Rs 500. Other fees: elephant ride, adult Rs 200, child Rs 100; pony ride for children under 12 Rs 25
voyage.content: Colombo's zoo has a wide variety of animals, birds, and reptiles from all over the world. See lion show, every day 4-4:15PM; elephant show, every day 4:30-4:55PM.

voyage.name: Viharamahadevi Park
voyage.content: It is the largest, oldest and most colourful park situated in the heart of Colombo, just opposite the colonial style Town Hall building.

voyage.name: Attidiya Bird Sanctuary
voyage.content: A beautiful marshland, rich with natural biodiversity and a resting place for many types of birds. The vegetation is dominated by sedge and grasses including Rhyuchospora rubra and Panicum repens. Around 43 species of waterfowl live in the area. Most common among them are Indian Shag (Phalaerocorox fuscicollis), and the Blue breasted Banded Rail (Rallus striatus). If you are an enthusiastic bird watcher or an eco fri

voyage.name: Sri Lanka Planetarium
voyage.content: Established in 1965. English shows on the last Saturday of the month at 2PM.

voyage.name: Gordon Gardens
voyage.content: About 16,000 m². The gardens have an amazing variety of trees.

voyage.name: Colombo Racecourse
voyage.address: Cinnamon Gardens, Philip Gunewardena Mawatha, Colombo 07
voyage.content: In 2012 it was redeveloped as the Colombo Racecourse Sports Complex to become the first International rugby union ground in Sri Lanka to host all the national rugby union side's home matches.

voyage.name: Royal College Sports Complex
voyage.address: 10, Sri Lanka Foundation Mawatha, Off Independence Avenue, Colombo 07

voyage.name: Sugathadasa Stadium
voyage.address: Arthur de Silva Mawatha or Prince of Wales Ave, Colombo 14

voyage.name: Nelum Pokuna Theatre
voyage.content: Performing arts theatre.

voyage.name: Barefoot
voyage.content: This handicraft shop has a wide range of good quality souvenirs and handmade items: clothes, bags and children toys, from some of the most beautifully-coloured fabric you've ever seen. While the biggest outlet is at Galle Road, there are smaller outlets at the Dutch Hospital and 41 Pedlar Street.

voyage.name: Crescat Boulevard
voyage.content: An up-market shopping mall. Though it is fairly small, it contains a food court on the basement floor.

voyage.name: Lakmedura
voyage.content: Gift shop.

voyage.name: Lakpahana
voyage.content: A non-profit organization run by the craftsman association of Sri Lanka with assistance from the government. Offers all handicrafts and gemstone jewellery. Unique metalware, wood carvings, silver jewellery, batik, textile products and other crafts.

voyage.name: Liberty Plaza
voyage.content: Similar to Majestic City but smaller. You can find various items such as clothing, CDs and DVDs.

voyage.name: Majestic City
voyage.content: In Kollupitiya on Galle Road has a wide variety of clothing outlets, including a sub-branch of Odel, at very good prices, as well as various electrical goods and toy shops. It's pleasantly air-conditioned and includes a food court on the ground floor.

voyage.name: Odel
voyage.content: A stylish department store, with its very own Delifrance outlet, clothing, houseware, sporting goods, books and movies, as well as Delight – for sweet indulgences from chocolates to exotic nuts.

voyage.name: Paradise Road
voyage.content: A shop with a small café in a British colonial style building where antiques, home décor items and art can be viewed or purchased.

voyage.name: The Pettah Market
voyage.content: Fruits to clothes to electronics at wholesale prices. You have to bargain extensively and it is recommended that you take a local you trust along with you. Even if you don't buy anything, Pettah, or Colombo 11 is an experience in itself being a very typical, loud and crowded oriental market place full of all sorts of odds, ends and junk. Each street in the market has its own speciality, for example, in 1st Cross Stre

voyage.name: Caveman Redux
voyage.content: A tranquil boutique dedicated to natural health, beauty, and wellness. Caveman Redux offers an extensive selection of essential oils, base oils, floral waters, plant extracts, dietary supplements, and raw natural ingredients for homemade skincare and wellness rituals.

voyage.name: New Yarl Eat House
voyage.price: A lunch for one including a full crab costs around Rs 400
voyage.content: It serves traditional Jaffna style rice and curries with excellent value for money crabs.

voyage.name: The Cricket Club Cafe
voyage.content: This cafe is a must for any cricket lover. The walls are covered in autographed memorabilia and photos with sports (usually cricket) being screened on all the TVs scattered throughout the rooms. They serve authentic Aussie cuisine and a wide variety of drinks. The bar is named after Donald Bradman.

voyage.name: The Gallery Cafe
voyage.content: Wonderful atmosphere in beautiful building - designed by famous Sri Lankan architect Geoffrey Bawa. Large food menu featuring many international dishes, decadent desserts and extensive cocktail menu.

voyage.name: The Lagoon
voyage.address: The Cinnamon Grand Hotel, 77 Galle Road
voyage.content: This restaurant focuses primarily on seafood with colourful Sri Lankan flavours. The friendly, professional staff create an enjoyable dining experience.

voyage.name: Mango Tree
voyage.content: One of the finest restaurants in the city. North Indian Cuisine, full of innovative dishes. Service is occasionally slow.

voyage.name: The Palmyrah Restaurant
voyage.content: Serves Jaffna style cuisine which is difficult to find outside of Northern Sri Lanka

voyage.name: 168 Seafood Palace
voyage.content: Serves excellent Chinese food and seafood dishes. Prices start at Rs 250. but some prices depend on weight (e.g. crabs). The service is very good.

voyage.name: Arunthathee Vihaar Vegetarian Family Restaurant
voyage.content: Vegetarian-only Indian Restaurant in Downtown Colombo. Serves authentic Indian food at very good prices.

voyage.name: Thalis Restaurant
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant, serves South Indian cuisine.

voyage.name: Nihonbashi Main Restaurant
voyage.content: There are three Nihonbashi outlets in Colombo. A sushi bar at Odel and an outlet at the Hilton Colombo Residence are the other two. The main restaurant is an airy and spacious restaurant with a blend of modern and traditional in design consisting of 8 private dining rooms also a dine-in wine room. Nihonbashi is owned and run by Tokyo-born Dharshan Munidasa, a self-taught chef.

voyage.name: Graze Kitchen
voyage.content: Features an array of ethnic cuisine like Chinese, Japanese, Sri Lankan, and Italian served in an interactive fashion.

voyage.name: Ginza Hohsen
voyage.content: A Japanese restaurant with a sushi bar, tatami rooms and teppanyaki.

voyage.name: The London Grill
voyage.content: As the name suggests this restaurant is very British. It probably has the best ambiance of all, and the food is just great.

voyage.name: California Grill
voyage.content: This is a fine dining restaurant on the rooftop level of the hotel. It offers panoramic views of the Galle Face marina. The food, mostly US-style grills and premium seafood, is excellent too.

voyage.name: Royal Thai
voyage.content: Located at the Cinnamon Lakeside Hotel is an authentic Thai restaurant offering the usual favourites, such as Tom Yam and Chicken Pandan leaves.

voyage.name: The Ministry of Crab
voyage.content: The Ministry of Crab serves the best crabs in Sri Lanka. Crabs are priced by the size and a kilo of crab costs around Rs 6500. They also serve their house speciality sweet tea with soda. One of the most expensive restaurants in Colombo, but it is definitely worth it.

voyage.name: Pegasus Reef Hotel
voyage.content: Beachside resort offering air-conditioned Deluxe and Premium rooms with balconies or terraces. Features an outdoor swimming pool, gym, tennis and squash courts, nature trail, children's play area, and on-site seafood restaurants and bars.

voyage.name: Fairway Colombo Hotel
voyage.content: The 4-star city hotel featuring en-suite rooms and multi-room suites with air conditioning, hot showers, Wi-Fi, flat-screen TVs, kettles, and safety deposit boxes; some units include balconies. Amenities include a bistro, rooftop restaurant with an outdoor bar, meeting spaces, and guest laundry service.

voyage.name: Parisare Homestay
voyage.content: This is a lovely home with a wonderful hostess, but they have only 3 rooms so prior reservation essential. In affluent Cinnamon Gardens neighbourhood which is 5km from Fort Station (20 minutes by car or 40 minutes by bus)

voyage.name: Miracle City Inn Hostel
voyage.content: Cheery hostel with white exterior and a rooftop terrace that will give you a full view of Colombo. Has a library, games, shared kitchen, comfy beds, and clean bathrooms.

voyage.name: C1 Colombo Fort
voyage.content: Hotel that is mostly up on the 4th floor of a building (with good viewsǃ). Strong wifi. Breakfast buffet is approx. Rs 370 additional.

voyage.name: Sapphire Hotel
voyage.content: 5 minutes away from the ocean. Has an on-site restaurant and bar. Each room includes air-conditioning, 24-hour room service, and satellite television. Has two reception halls for those wishing to host a convention or wedding reception. Reservations are required.

voyage.name: Hotel Clarion
voyage.content: All rooms are equipped with air-conditioning, a TV with cable channels and are wheelchair accessible. Also in the hotel is the 180 restaurant, a fitness centre with steam room and a business centre. The Clarion is a bit far from the central city: it will generally take at least 45 minutes to travel to the centre, with possible 30-minute delays from heavy traffic.

voyage.name: Hotel Galadari
voyage.content: Has 446 rooms, including 23 suites. There are special executive level and handicap rooms. There are a variety of dining facilities in the hotel to suit different palates. Als has spa and fitness facilities.

voyage.name: Hotel Janaki
voyage.content: This 3-star hotel offers its guests rooms with air-conditioning, cable/satellite TV, and a room safe. There is a restaurant and bar on site, with 24-hour room service.

voyage.name: Garden Guest House
voyage.content: This three-room guest house offers its visitors attached bathrooms, free internet services and laundry facilities. The staff at the guest house can also arrange island tours and airport pick-up.

voyage.name: Palm Village Hotel
voyage.content: Located between the city and the airport, has 50 air-conditioned rooms with either a balcony or a terrace. Has a restaurant and bar, as well as a jewellery and souvenir shop.

voyage.name: Hotel Renuka & Renuka City Hotel
voyage.content: These sister hotels offer their guests comfortable rooms and friendly service. Each room is equipped with flat screen television with local and cable channels, 24-hour room service, in-room safes and internet connection. The hotels have one of the most famous restaurants in Sri Lanka, the Palmyrah, which serves authentic Sri Lankan cuisine. A popular dish is Iso Thel Dala, spicy prawns sautéed with onions and tomato.

voyage.name: Mount Lavinia Hotel
voyage.content: This is a colonial heritage hotel dating back to early 1800s. It consists of 210 rooms inclusive of colonial, ocean view, and suites. The ocean view rooms are a bit dated. There are 6 restaurants and bars as well as facilities to host business events and weddings. The dinner and breakfast buffets are spectacular.

voyage.name: Galle Face Hotel
voyage.content: A famous, old fashioned colonial style grand hotel. Most rooms come with a view of the ocean or the Galle Face Green. The hotel also has a variety of restaurants on site to choose from, including: The 1864 and Verandah. Spa and butler services are also available for guests.

voyage.name: Hotel Nippon
voyage.content: Decent rooms fitted with air-con, cable TV, etc. It is located in a prime location in the city close to all essential sight seeing spots. Some of its facilities and services are restaurant, and bar.

voyage.name: The Havelock Place Bungalow
voyage.content: A boutique hotel, consisting of two restored colonial homes. Tastefully decorated using antique colonial furniture. Provides wireless Internet, pool, jacuzzi, restaurants.

voyage.name: Uga Residence
voyage.address: 20 Park street, Slave Island, Colombo 2, Sri Lanka
voyage.content: Near major shopping centres and business establishments. Decked with colonial touches, like antique furniture and high ceilings. Rooms are equipped with Jacuzzi, DVD player and refrigerator.

voyage.name: Tintagel
voyage.address: 65 Rosmead Place, Cinnamon Gardens, Colombo 7, Sri Lanka
voyage.content: Situated in Rosmead Place. Once a stately home to the political Bandaranaike family. The 10 elegant suites have high ceilings and timber floors. They open to a private courtyard, balcony, or separate lounge area. Each suite also has king-size beds with Egyptian cotton sheets, and a bathroom with a rain shower and bath.

voyage.name: The Kingsbury Colombo
voyage.content: Has 250 rooms, all with views of the city or Indian Ocean. Various onsite restaurants and cafes on site. 24-hour room service, fitness facilities and spa services.

voyage.name: Cinnamon Grand Colombo
voyage.content: Has a spa and meeting facilities.

voyage.name: Taj Samudra
voyage.address: 25, Galle Face Centre Road, Kollupitiya, Colombo 3
voyage.content: A variety of rooms; they range from standards with views of the sea and pool to presidential suites with separate dining and dressing areas. Also equipped with a fitness centre, book shop and swimming pool. There are also a variety of restaurants ranging from casual in dress to fine dining.

voyage.name: Cinnamon Lakeside Colombo
voyage.content: As of Dec 2012, the rooms were quite tired and are in need of renovation. The price they ask does not reflect this. Despite this, the service is good and otherwise is a reasonable place to stay.

voyage.name: Colombo Courtyard Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Has a wine cellar, a rooftop café, cloud café, spa, pool side dining options. The Scarlet restaurant offers European, Mediterranean and Asian food.

voyage.name: Shangri-La Hotel
voyage.content: Luxury class hotel tower standing out among the mushrooming skyline of Colombo.
